archetypes.name: oos-state
archetypes.rationale: The diff changes OOS_PENDING, disposition-gate, sentinel, and PR-creation control flow across multiple runtime paths.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate the end-to-end OOS state machine across scripts/ship-pr.sh, python/ship.py, skills/implement/SKILL.md, and oos-pipeline.md. Check whether accepted OOS can still be skipped, double-filed, prematurely marked satisfied, or allowed through to PR creation before checkpoint evidence exists. Pay special attention to sentinel recovery, all-already-filed design OOS, repo-unavailable and fork carve-outs, and failed materialization branches. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: manifest-bridge
archetypes.rationale: A new helper translates external implementer manifest JSON into markdown OOS artifacts and is easy to get subtly wrong.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review materialize-manifest-oos.sh and its invocation sites for manifest parsing, idempotency, monotonic OOS_N allocation, duplicate-title handling, malformed or missing fields, and failure semantics. Verify the helper's behavior matches the documented contract and that step2, ship-pr, and Python callers fail open or closed in the intended cases. Consider whether manifest-only OOS can be lost due to jq errors, unreadable files, empty arrays, or security-routed observations. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: bash-runtime
archetypes.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial Bash with set -euo pipefail, jq, awk, redirection, and state-machine interactions.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect the added and modified Bash for runtime hazards under the repository's supported shell assumptions. Focus on quoting, unset variables, set -e interactions, command-substitution failures, function ordering, temp/log file handling, executable checks, and whether captured exit codes survive as intended. Include scripts/ship-pr.sh, step2-implement.sh, materialize-manifest-oos.sh, and the new harness in scope. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: python-parity
archetypes.rationale: Python ship.py is intended to mirror bash ship-pr behavior for design-path resolution and OOS materialization.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare python/ship.py behavior against the bash ship-pr OOS path described in the plan and implemented in scripts/ship-pr.sh. Check ordering around PR body composition, manifest materialization, ctx.oos_pending, accepted-file size checks, _oos_gate invocation, design-export and DESIGN_TMPDIR resolution, and run-dir ndjson fallback. Look for semantic drift between Python and Bash drivers that could produce different OOS filing or PR creation outcomes. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: public-redaction
archetypes.rationale: Manifest-derived OOS text may be written to public issue bodies and committed logs, so sanitization and security routing matter.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review all new paths that transform manifest or session-derived text into OOS markdown, issue bodies, larch-log evidence, execution issues, and security-routed audit files. Check whether secrets, internal URLs, PII, injected headings, and security-only findings are consistently sanitized or withheld from public filing surfaces. Verify the focus-area security predicate is compatible with the gate and does not misclassify prose or non-security labels. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
